cards.text: Isaiah the prophet has had hard news for God's people. They ran to Egypt for help without asking the LORD, and when He told them repentance and rest would save them, they said no thanks, we'll flee on horses (Isaiah 30:2, 15-16). So when the prophet says "Therefore," friend, I'd be hiding behind my own mustache.

cards.question: After all that running and refusing, the prophet says "Therefore." What does the LORD long to do for His people?

cards.text: He rises to show them compassion, for the LORD is a just God. Then the prophet says who is blessed.

cards.question: The LORD longs to be gracious to His people. Who does the prophet call blessed?

answers.text: All who make their own plans

cards.text: Waiting? Friend, I stare at my oven light like it owes me money. Then the prophet speaks straight to the people in Zion who dwell in Jerusalem: "you will weep no more."

cards.question: When the people in Jerusalem cry for help, the LORD hears them but stays silent.

cards.text: But hard times will still come: the Lord will give them the bread of adversity and the water of affliction.

cards.question: Even in those hard days, something changes about the people's Teacher. What is it?

answers.text: He will no longer hide Himself
He will leave them on their own
He will only speak in dreams

cards.text: With their own eyes they'll see Him. And whether they turn to the right or to the left, their ears will hear a command behind them.

cards.question: Whether God's people turn right or left, the command they hear behind them shows them the way to walk.

cards.text: And the command is, "This is the way. Walk in it." Friend, that's the voice for anybody who's ever missed an exit, then three more, still SURE they know a shortcut.

cards.question: So the people will do something with their silver-plated idols and gold-plated images. What will they do?

cards.text: They'll desecrate those idols and throw them away like menstrual cloths, saying to them, "Be gone!" Then the prophet turns to the seed they've sown in the ground.

cards.question: The LORD will send ___ for the seed they have sown in the ground.
Even after the LORD sends rain for their seed, the food from their land stays thin and scarce.

cards.text: On that day their cattle will graze in open pastures, and the oxen and donkeys will eat salted fodder, winnowed with shovel and pitchfork. Friend, all those years in the back of a junk drawer I lived on DUST, and these donkeys get it SALTED.

cards.question: There's water coming too. Where will streams of water flow from?

answers.text: Every high mountain and raised hill

cards.text: Those streams will flow in the day of great slaughter, when the towers fall. And the moon will be as bright as the sun, with the sun SEVEN times brighter.

cards.question: The moon will shine as bright as the sun on the day the LORD ___ the wounds of His people.

cards.text: That's the day the LORD binds up the brokenness of His people and heals the wounds He has inflicted.
Then the prophet says, "Behold," and the Name of the LORD comes from afar, with burning anger and dense smoke. His lips are full of fury, and His tongue is like a consuming fire.

cards.question: The LORD comes to sift His own people in a sieve of destruction.

cards.text: It's the nations He sifts, and His breath is like a rushing torrent that rises to the neck. He bridles the jaws of the peoples to lead them astray.

cards.question: Then the prophet turns back to God's people. What will they do?

answers.text: Sing as on a holy festival night

cards.text: Their hearts will rejoice like someone walking to the music of a flute, going up to the mountain of the LORD, to the Rock of Israel. Picture your best commute ever, then delete the traffic.

cards.question: The LORD will make His majestic voice heard and reveal His mighty arm, striking in angry wrath. What comes with it?

cards.text: Then the prophet names a nation: Assyria, a powerful empire. And the voice of the LORD is coming for it.

cards.question: What will happen to Assyria at the voice of the LORD?

cards.text: He will strike them with His scepter, stroke after stroke of the rod of punishment, as He battles with weapons brandished.

cards.question: With every stroke of the LORD's rod on Assyria, tambourines and lyres will sound.

cards.text: Then the prophet names a place: Topheth, in the Valley of Ben-hinnom (Jeremiah 7:31). It has long been prepared, made ready for the king, and its funeral pyre is deep and wide, with plenty of fire and wood.

cards.question: Topheth's funeral pyre is set ablaze by the ___ of the LORD, like a torrent of burning sulfur.
